reference_answer: Finite summation by parts gives sum_{i=0}^n p_i/2^(i+1)=2+sum_{i=0}^{n-1}g_i/2^(i+1)-p_n/2^(n+1). The source supplies a polynomial bound for p_n, so the endpoint vanishes and both series converge absolutely. Hence Pi=2+G; D=2Pi=4+2G. A rational shift and a nonzero rational scaling preserve rationality and irrationality in both directions. The equivalence supplies no irrationality theorem for the actual primes. Unbounded/nonperiodic integer coefficients may have rational dyadic sums; unlike binary digits they permit carries. This is an existing source identity, not a new transfer result.
